prompt: Adult men in a city have a mean height of $68$ inches. A researcher plans to take a random sample of $50$ men and compute the sample mean $\bar{x}$. What is the mean of the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$, in inches?
hint: Sample means vary from sample to sample, but they are centered somewhere. The sample mean is an unbiased estimator.

hints.text: Sample means vary from sample to sample, but they are centered somewhere. The sample mean is an unbiased estimator.
Unbiased means $\mu_{\bar{x}} = \mu$ for any sample size, so the answer is the population mean given in the problem.
The mean of the sampling distribution is $68$ inches, the same as the population mean.

explanation: The sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ is the distribution of sample means over all possible samples of size 50.
Its center is the population mean: $\mu_{\bar{x}} = \mu = 68$.
Sample size changes the SPREAD of sample means, not their center.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why it is unbiased
steps: Some samples will have a mean above 68, some below, just by chance.
There is no reason for the sample means to lean one way, so they balance out at 68.
That balance point is the mean of the sampling distribution: 68 inches.
